Container.Name: Caddy
Container.Overview: Caddy 2 web server and reverse proxy (official Caddy plus the caddy-dns/cloudflare module, built by CaddyBuilds) with automatic HTTPS. Certificates are proven through Cloudflare DNS, so port 80 is not needed for certificates.[br][br] Unraid's own web UI uses ports 80/443, so the defaults map Caddy to host ports 1880 (HTTP) and 18443 (HTTPS); forward external 80/443 on your router to those.[br][br] The Caddyfile lives in the Caddyfile folder; certificates in the Data folder (back this up). Apply Caddyfile changes without downtime with: docker exec -w /etc/caddy Caddy caddy reload
Container.Requires: Create the Caddyfile (in the Caddyfile folder below) BEFORE the first start. Needs an env file at the path in Extra Parameters (chmod 600) containing CADDY_CF_API_TOKEN=<scoped Cloudflare API token with Zone:Read + DNS:Edit>; reference it in the Caddyfile as {env.CADDY_CF_API_TOKEN}. The env file is read when the container is created: after changing it, use Edit then Apply (or Force Update), not just Restart. Stop any other reverse proxy that holds the same host ports first.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: Host port the router forwards external port 80 to. Used for HTTP->HTTPS redirects (and Let's Encrypt HTTP challenges, if ever used).

Config.Name: HTTPS Port
Config.Description: Host port the router forwards external port 443 to.

Config.Name: HTTPS Port (HTTP/3)
Config.Description: Optional: HTTP/3 (QUIC). Only useful if the router also forwards UDP 443 to this port.

Config.Name: Caddyfile folder
Config.Description: Folder that holds the Caddyfile. Mounted as a folder (not a single file) so edits are seen without recreating the container.

Config.Name: Data (certificates)
Config.Description: Certificates, ACME account and keys. Back this up; losing it means re-requesting every certificate.
